the envelope membrane of Chlamydomonads is a highly dynamic membrane that has the ability to change its biochemical properties, and that this is a mechanism for the compartmentalization of the chloroplast.

the chloroplasts are a highly organized organelle that is involved in the biogenesis of chloroplasts and photosynthesis in plants.

chloroplasts are not just a simple compartment for the synthesis of chlorophyll and the assembly of photosynthetic complexes, but they are also highly organized organelles for the synthesis and assembly of the photosynthesizing machinery and the import of proteins from the cytoplasm.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the chloroplast is a highly compartmentalized organelle that is specialized in the synthesis and import of proteins that are required for the biogenesis and function of the photosynthesizing thylakoid membrane.
chloroplasts contain novel membrane systems that are involved in de novo biogenesis of photosystem II, the import of proteins from the cytoplasm, and the synthesis of chlorophyll.
